newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rate up on weekend covering.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rate up on weekend covering.

text.p: Philippine interbank call loan rates rose slightly to an average of 11.125 percent from 11.0625 as banks covered three days of reserve position, traders said.
Done rates on Monday ranged from 11.500 to 11.0625 percent, with volume rising to 21.1 billion from 14.445 billion pesos.
Dealers said the market could tighten by midweek when the the Central Bank's dollar sales last Friday impacts on the market.
Those dollar sales are to be delivered only on Tuesday, which would effectively drain pesos from banks which bought them.
In the secondary market, dealers said there was not much activity since there were few sellers of T-Bills on expectations interest rates would dip further.
One dealer said the three-month bill was being offered at 11.525 percent; the six-month at 11.85; and the one-year at 12.600. - LILIAN KARUNUNGAN (632) 841-8937
